generation.subject: /CN=GrapheneOS/
generation.subjectBasis: GrapheneOS/script 09d651841b55e42b9cee7392f0ce29ebda8c8fb5 generate-keys (blob 5c38a53eeda4eb16c55bd3a3ad776a3cb1d6349e): CN=GrapheneOS; make_key $key "/CN=$CN/". This is the retained existing pattern's public subject; no RoseOS or Frankel certificate subject is retained in this repository, so no match with the existing Frankel keys is claimed.
generation.note: Non-interactive form of generate-keys + encrypt-keys: make_key reads the passphrase from stdin and writes scrypt-encrypted PKCS#8 DER (it always exits 1 through its EXIT trap); the AVB key is generated with openssl genrsa 4096, its public key extracted by avbtool (which needs the unencrypted key, as in generate-keys before encryption), then encrypted with openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -scrypt using the passphrase file (encrypt-keys form); the unencrypted intermediate stays in the owner-only workspace and is overwritten and removed after encryption. Nothing runs until the installed tool identities are measured.

localProof.admissionBasis: OCT30-INFRA-S016: Fold #191 (FOLD-TOOL-PROOF-001 correction), the Models Product's minimal managed-host helper (pinned script bytes, fixed PATH resolution, host package manager identity and integrity; no custom cryptography), merged as b4e317ad. Its test suite runs in Release verification from this change; any other helper bytes refuse.

excluded.basis: Chief scope correction: the custom-crypto (pure-Python OpenPGP/RSA, ELF closure) helper is not an admitted Fold proof regardless of main ancestry or green CI

localProof.specBasis: The original builder source tree (os/release-pipeline/frankel.json host.sourceRoot) at each script's pinned project path (development, script, external/avb); verify_local checks the bytes there against the pinned git blob and sha256 above, so a wrong root refuses.

Recorded only; execution must reread metadata and these are never reapplied by this adapter.

keyInventory.basis: A single dedicated Models identity; no Fold or Agent key is reused.

trust.basisNote: tree and blob ids read from the pinned commit through a supported blob-less fetch of the canonical manifest remote (OCT30-INFRA-S012 adjustment, 00:05 full-checkout approval); the whole local linux-x86 directory (425 entries: 189 files, 31 executables, 205 in-tree relative symlinks) is recomputed as a git tree before metadata and again before generation; no host checksum list, index or installed hash is trusted

keytool.requiredObservation: none exported: the local tree recomputation is the identity check (S011 receipt values are not used)

generation.note: keytool takes the store and key passwords from the passphrase file (-storepass:file / -keypass:file, the documented JDK keytool password-file form); nothing secret is in argv or the environment. The store is reloaded twice (exportcert, list -v) and its public listing and certificate are checked before import; the public files are then removed and only keystore.p12 and passphrase remain. keytool runs by its explicit pinned-tree path with a fresh minimal environment (PATH, LC_ALL, HOME only: no JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, _JAVA_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS, CLASSPATH or LD_*). The Models key bootstrap needs keytool only; APK signing tools (SDK apksigner.jar, aapt) stay separately unbound.

fold-rango-factory-v1.purpose: Rango factory-archive SSH signing identity: one new passphrase-encrypted Ed25519 key for ssh-keygen -Y sign -n "factory images" of rango-install-{build}.zip; never derived from or stored with the OS (OTA/AVB/APK) keys

ssh-keygen.requiredObservation: installed path, sha256 and version (OpenSSH >= 8.4 for SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force) of ssh-keygen on the builder, then the synthetic self-check, in an approved run

generation.note: scripts/factory_signing.py generate_key: ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -a 100 -C '' -f <workspace>/id_ed25519 with stdin closed, a new session, core dumps off, a 60 s timeout and environment exactly PATH, LANG, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force and SSH_ASKPASS=<pinned helper>; the passphrase is a random file read only by that helper. No passphrase in argv, environment, output or receipt.

access.policy: Proposed ceilings only: bootstrap access <= 4 h and secretAccessor <= 30 d after grant, enforced by the actual IAM conditions. These fields are filled only from an IAM readback of those exact expiries (with basis); while null they are not enforced, assumed or substituted and readiness refuses (access-unknown). Recorded expiries beyond the ceilings refuse (access-window).

missing: owner/security approval of the new identity (FOLD-FACTORY-IDENTITY proposal)
the two empty secret containers, created by the admin
time-boxed bootstrap access (secrets.get, versions.list, versions.add, 4 h) and secretAccessor (30 d) for the signer on those two containers only
measured ssh-keygen installed identity and version on the builder
fold-rango-factory-v1.importRecovery: The two-secret import is not atomic. Any uncertain or partial outcome (keys added but passphrase not, an add whose outcome is unknown) stops as recovery-needed and is journaled; every later run refuses on that journal (previous-attempt) and never regenerates a key or repeats an import. Recovery is a separate owner decision.

This is the retained existing pattern's public subject; no RoseOS or Frankel certificate subject is retained in this repository, so no match with the existing Frankel keys is claimed.
generation.note: Non-interactive form of generate-keys + encrypt-keys: make_key reads the passphrase from stdin and writes scrypt-encrypted PKCS#8 DER (it always exits 1 through its EXIT trap); the AVB key is generated with openssl genrsa 4096, its public key extracted by avbtool (which needs the unencrypted key, as in generate-keys before encryption), then encrypted with openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -scrypt using the passphrase file (encrypt-keys form); the unencrypted intermediate stays in the owner-only workspace and is overwritten and removed after encryption. Nothing runs until the installed tool identities are measured.

pro-blazer-factory-v1.purpose: Pixel 10 Pro (blazer) factory-archive SSH signing identity: one new passphrase-encrypted Ed25519 key for ssh-keygen -Y sign -n "factory images" of blazer-install-{build}.zip; never derived from or stored with any OS key

ssh-keygen.requiredObservation: installed path, sha256 and version (OpenSSH >= 8.4 for SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force) of ssh-keygen on the builder, then the synthetic self-check, in an approved run

generation.note: scripts/factory_signing.py generate_key: ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -a 100 -C '' -f <workspace>/id_ed25519 with stdin closed, a new session, core dumps off, a 60 s timeout and environment exactly PATH, LANG, SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force and SSH_ASKPASS=<pinned helper>; the passphrase is a random file read only by that helper. No passphrase in argv, environment, output or receipt.

access.policy: Proposed ceilings only: bootstrap access <= 4 h and secretAccessor <= 30 d after grant, enforced by the actual IAM conditions. These fields are filled only from an IAM readback of those exact expiries (with basis); while null they are not enforced, assumed or substituted and readiness refuses (access-unknown). Recorded expiries beyond the ceilings refuse (access-window).

time-boxed bootstrap access (secrets.get, versions.list, versions.add, 4 h) and secretAccessor (30 d) for the signer on those two containers only

pro-blazer-factory-v1.importRecovery: The two-secret import is not atomic. Any uncertain or partial outcome (keys added but passphrase not, an add whose outcome is unknown) stops as recovery-needed and is journaled; every later run refuses on that journal (previous-attempt) and never regenerates a key or repeats an import. Recovery is a separate owner decision.
